stem: Which statement is true regarding stimulant medication used to treat ADHD?

options.text: There is no weaning-off period required when stopping the medication
The dose is determined strictly by the child’s weight and does not vary
It is highly addictive when used in the prescribed dose for ADHD
It cures the underlying neurobiological cause of ADHD over time
It must always be tapered slowly to avoid withdrawal symptoms

explanation: There is no weaning-off period required because stimulant medications have a short half-life and can be stopped or restarted without gradual dose reduction.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because stimulant medications have a short half-life and can be stopped or restarted without gradual dose reduction.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the effective dose is individualised and may need adjustment, even though weight is considered when prescribing.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because stimulants used as prescribed for ADHD are not considered highly addictive in this context.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because stimulant medication treats ADHD symptoms rather than curing the underlying condition.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because stimulant medications do not usually require slow tapering to prevent withdrawal when used for ADHD.

source.hint: Think about the duration of the medication's effect in the body and how it is managed on weekends.
